site.title: Belgium Budget Builder
home.title: Where does Belgium's money go?
home.lede: Most of us have little sense of how big each part of the public budget is. This site shows the federal, social security and regional budgets of 2026 to scale, so you can see how the topics relate, how hard it is to land a budget, and what choices mean over the next ten years.
home.status: Under construction. Every figure will be sourced and reviewed before it is published.
map.title: Budget map
map.intro: Every rectangle is drawn to scale: twice the area means twice the money. Choose a government to see what it spends on.
map.transfersNote: Money one government passes on to another is shown only where it is finally spent, so nothing is counted twice.
outlook.title: Ten-year outlook
outlook.intro: What happens to the public debt if the budget stays as it is, or as you set it above. Rising pension and healthcare costs from an ageing population are included.
outlook.balanceChange: Your change to the yearly balance
outlook.chartLabel: Public debt as a share of GDP, {from} to {to}
outlook.interestRate: Average interest rate on the debt
outlook.caveat: This is simple arithmetic, not a forecast. It does not model how people and companies react to tax or spending changes, nor interest rates that change over time. Ageing costs follow the official Study Committee on Ageing report; changing pension or healthcare spending scales their projected increase in the same proportion.
ageing.title: The cost of ageing
ageing.intro: Compared with 2026, pensions and healthcare take a growing share of the economy, even if nothing else changes. These are the official projections of the Study Committee on Ageing; the extra cost is already included in the outlook above.
ageing.scaled: Your changes to pensions and healthcare in the map above also change this cost, in the same proportion.
ageing.chartLabel: Extra cost of ageing per year compared with 2026, in % of GDP, by pensions, healthcare and other, {from} to {to}
consequence.title: What this change means: {name}
consequence.whereNote: Spread in proportion to the size of each part. A real reform chooses where to cut.
consequence.offset: matched by equal receipts, so cutting it alone saves nothing
consequence.howIntro: Spending like this changes through these levers. Each one is felt by someone different.
